stories.title: Leucine does more than build muscle. It powers up your cells
stories.summary: The essential amino acid leucine can boost cellular energy production by protecting key proteins on mitochondria from being destroyed. The discovery reveals a new connection between nutrition and metabolism that could eventually lead to new approaches for metabolic disorders and cancer.

stories.title: This protective enzyme could help stop fatty liver disease from getting worse
stories.summary: Scientists have identified an enzyme that may act as a natural defense against the worsening of fatty liver disease, which affects an estimated 100 million Americans.

stories.title: Vitamin C linked to fewer deaths in blood disorder trial
stories.summary: Vitamin C may do more than support the immune system. In a phase 2 trial of people with precancerous or low risk blood cancers, daily vitamin C did not slow abnormal cell growth, but it was linked to favorable changes in inflammation and fewer serious complications.

stories.title: Your gut may be making a molecule that raises Alzheimer’s risk
stories.summary: Scientists have linked a gut bacterial compound called ImP to greater Alzheimer’s risk, harmful brain protein buildup, and faster cognitive decline. The finding raises the possibility that reducing ImP in the blood could one day help slow or prevent dementia.

stories.title: An Ebola treatment center was burned down as the death toll in Congo passes 4,000
stories.summary: Congo's Ebola outbreak has killed more than 4,000 people, authorities said, as they struggle to contain what has become the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history.

stories.title: Antenatal interventions to support newborn survival: updates for the Lives Saved Tool
stories.summary: Antenatal care strategies encompass a series of interventions delivered to expectant mothers to optimise both their health outcomes and those of their neonate.

stories.title: Association of long-term depressive burden with incident cardiometabolic multimorbidity: a prospective study in middle-aged and older adults across three continents
stories.summary: Cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) is a growing concern as global population ages. Although baseline depression is a recognised risk factor for chronic diseases, the dynamic and cumulative effect of depression on CMM remains unclear.

stories.title: Beyond Longitudinal Sampling: Translating Sexually Transmissible Enteric Infection Research Into Gastrointestinal Diagnostic Pathways
stories.summary: Abdulrasak M, Bagger-Jörgensen H.

stories.title: Cancer stem cells have an “energy addiction” scientists may be able to exploit
stories.summary: High-risk MDS stem cells appear to have an unexpected “energy addiction,” relying far more heavily than healthy blood-forming cells on a molecule called NAD. Disrupting this energy pathway selectively weakened the cancer-driving cells, revealing a potential new target for treatment.

stories.title: Cost-effectiveness of community-based artificial intelligence screening for retinopathy of prematurity
stories.summary: Retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) is one of the leading causes of childhood blindness globally, but particularly in middle-income countries, where neonatal survival has improved faster than access to specialist ophthalmic care.

stories.title: Distinguishing task shifting from task sharing through the delegating provider's presence or absence: proposed operational definitions
stories.summary: Task shifting and task sharing are strategies for redistributing healthcare responsibilities to optimise healthcare services.

stories.title: Equity-focused investment strategies to reduce maternal mortality in the Philippines: a subnational analysis using EQUIST
stories.summary: Despite sustained national progress in maternal and child health, maternal mortality in the Philippines remains uneven across regions and socioeconomic groups.

stories.title: From hope to health: improving sexual and reproductive health knowledge among adolescent orphan girls through the 'HopeBox' intervention in Bangladesh
stories.summary: Orphaned adolescent girls face critical barriers to accessing accurate sexual and reproductive health (SRH) knowledge, which predisposes them to risky sexual behaviours and their consequences.

stories.title: Gaza: WHO appeals for massive aid influx ahead of winter
stories.summary: Repeated delays in bringing lifesaving medicines, prosthetics and more from Israel into Gaza risk having devastating consequences on Palestinians who urgently need them in the war-torn enclave, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) said on Friday.

stories.title: How big is Pennsylvania’s measles outbreak?
stories.summary: News of a fifth measles death in Pennsylvania underscores a longstanding issue about the disease. The full scope of the outbreak ,  in the state and in the country , …

stories.title: Influence of environmental, economic, dietary, and behavioural factors on high myopia onset in children: a 4-year large-scale cohort study
stories.summary: High myopia (HM) has become a major global public health concern, leading to irreversible vision loss and a growing socioeconomic burden.

stories.title: Multi-omics Mendelian randomisation reveals distinct molecular drivers of pathological myopia complications vs simple myopia
stories.summary: Pathological myopia complications are leading causes of irreversible blindness, yet the molecular mechanisms distinguishing them from simple myopia remain poorly understood.

stories.title: Nationwide Surveillance and Control Measures during Large Measles Outbreak, Bangladesh, 2026
stories.summary: Nationwide surveillance in Bangladesh during April 2-May 27, 2026, identified a total of 67,079 suspected and 8,834 confirmed measles cases across 8 administrative divisions. Among suspected cases, 472 deaths were reported, and 88 deaths were reported among confirmed cases.

stories.title: Nearly 6 in 10 people with high blood pressure don’t know they have it
stories.summary: Nearly 6 in 10 people with high blood pressure in a large England study had never been diagnosed or treated, and half of those already taking medication still had elevated readings.

stories.title: Northern India Braces for Toxic Winter Pollution, Despite Improved Delhi Plan
stories.summary: Rural farm fires and Diwali fireworks likely to trigger pollution emergencies in northern India during late autumn and early winter, despite the rollout of new pollution control measures in the capital city territory.

stories.title: October 1 ushered in a new era in U.S. foreign aid. What's the plan? Will it work?
stories.summary: The America First strategy asks for a Memorandum of Understanding as a condition for healthcare and development aid. It's been praised for promoting self-reliance but criticized for its conditions.

stories.title: Opinion: I treated heat stroke at the NYC Marathon. Marathons need to prepare for a climate-changed world
stories.summary: A doctor’s request to marathons: Let’s make evidence-based medical plans ,  especially for extreme heat.

stories.title: Postnatal interventions to support newborn survival: updates for the Lives Saved Tool
stories.summary: The period immediately after birth represents a highly vulnerable time for newborns, particularly in contexts without access to high-quality secondary care for small and/or sick newborns.

stories.title: Prevalence of abnormal spirometry and correlates of lung function decline among a population in rural Uganda
stories.summary: Chronic lung disease, which is the third leading cause of death globally, places a disproportionate burden of morbidity and mortality on sub-Saharan Africa, where limited infrastructure results in a lack of understanding of how lung function changes over time, whether it varies among susceptible...

stories.title: Scientists may have found a “unifying theory” of chronic fatigue
stories.summary: Scientists found that five seemingly unrelated conditions, including long Covid, ME/CFS, and PTSD, may disrupt many of the same biological networks involved in immunity, metabolism, and cellular energy.

stories.title: Serologic Assessment of Public Health Action Needed for Trachoma, Coastal Ecuador, 2021-2024
stories.summary: We evaluated the probability of needing public health actions against trachoma in Esmeraldas Province, Ecuador, by estimating seroconversion rates of Chlamydia trachomatis plasma gene protein 3 IgG in children.

stories.title: The burden and long-term outcomes of diagnosed and underdiagnosed COPD across diverse communities from high-income, middle-income, and low-income countries: the Prospective Urban Rural Epidemiology (PURE) study
stories.summary: Airflow obstruction detected on spirometry is a hallmark of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and is needed for the diagnosis of COPD. Sparse data in high-income countries (HICs) have reported high prevalence of underdiagnosed COPD with poor clinical outcomes.

stories.title: The Impermanence of Public Health Gains-Lessons Learned from Measles Resurgence, Bangladesh, 2026
stories.summary: The global resurgence of measles is a major public health concern. After the success of its Expanded Programme on Immunization, Bangladesh experienced a measles resurgence in 2026.

stories.title: Tracking the impact of maternal health service coverage on maternal mortality across 137 low- and middle-income countries in the progress toward Sustainable Development Goals
stories.summary: Achieving Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 3, particularly targets 3.1 (reducing the global maternal mortality ratio (MMR) to less than 70 per 100,000 live births) and 3.8 (universal health coverage), requires sustained reductions in maternal mortality and equitable access to essential maternal...

stories.title: Validating DigiHEALTHQUAL for measuring digital health effects on service quality in outpatient care in Germany
stories.summary: The adoption of digital health solutions (DHS) in outpatient care is hindered by uncertainty regarding their non-clinical effects and a lack of validated instruments for standardized evaluation.

stories.title: Weak sunlight can still damage your DNA, scientists warn
stories.summary: Weak sunlight can still damage skin DNA if you spend enough time outdoors, according to a landmark Australian study. Even UV doses too low to cause visible redness triggered cellular damage that could accumulate over time and contribute to skin cancer risk.

stories.title: West Bank Healthcare: Closed Roads, Empty Treasury & Doctors Detained
stories.summary: ISRAELI-OCCUPIED WEST BANK – The oxygen mask slipped from three-month-old Ahmad Zaid’s face. He was in his father’s arms, in front of a closed Israeli military gate blocking the road between Deir Ammar refugee camp, northwest of Ramallah, where the family lives, and the city of Ramallah, with a...

stories.title: 'It's a nightmare.' Former refugee, professor on Trump's new Medicaid policy
stories.summary: Starting Oct. 1, many immigrants who are here legally lose their Medicaid coverage because of the Republican budget bill passed last year.

stories.title: 1 in 13 adults under 30 already had hidden artery plaque
stories.summary: More than half of 16,000 apparently healthy adults had signs of atherosclerosis, with arterial plaques already detectable in about 1 in 13 people ages 18 to 29. Researchers say directly imaging the arteries could reveal hidden cardiovascular disease years or even decades before symptoms appear.

stories.title: A case for eliminating Widal testing for enteric fever, India
stories.summary: Walia K, Gopalakrishnan R, Rupali P, Rodrigues C, Ramasubramanian V, Balaji V, Ohri V, Dang N, Wattal C, Reddy H, Bansal N, Singh H.

stories.title: A new California law bans child marriage. What's the global outlook on the practice?
stories.summary: The governor of California has signed into law a ban on child marriage. What is the status of other efforts to ban the practice? And do bans prove effective?

stories.title: Accounting for heterogeneity in mosquito exposure to forecast chikungunya outbreaks in Reunion Island and Paraguay: a mathematical modelling study
stories.summary: Heterogeneity in mosquito exposure at a fine spatial scale is well documented but often neglected in mathematical models of arbovirus transmission, particularly for real-time forecasting.

stories.title: Age Differences in Pertussis Epidemics, New South Wales, Australia, 2015 and 2024
stories.summary: We compared data from the 2015 and 2024 pertussis epidemics in New South Wales, Australia. In 2024, we found twice as many notifications and a shift in distribution to older children.

stories.title: Alzheimer’s risk gene APOE4 may have a reversible weakness
stories.summary: The Alzheimer’s risk gene APOE4 may actively damage brain blood vessels and sabotage the cellular systems that remove harmful proteins.

stories.title: As CDC redesigns annual health survey, it removes questions about disabilities
stories.summary: Proposed changes to the federal government’s health survey would undercount Americans with disabilities, advocates say.

stories.title: Beyond the sycophantic vs. cold divide: towards flexible, emotionally intelligent agents to foster healthier human-AI interactions
stories.summary: Montag C, Spapé M, Wong DF, Wu H, Dexter JP, Xu CZ.

stories.title: Bundibugyo virus disease and the unfinished countermeasure agenda
stories.summary: Abrescia N, Capponi A, Maddaloni A, Molinaro G, D'Abbraccio M.

stories.title: Chlamydia psittaci Meningitis, Chile, 2023
stories.summary: We report a confirmed case of Chlamydia psittaci meningitis in Latin America, diagnosed in a 50-year-old farm worker from Chile. Diagnosis was established via cerebrospinal fluid quantitative real-time PCR and serology. The patient recovered after antimicrobial treatment.

stories.title: Clinical Characterization of Invasive Meningococcal Disease Epidemic, Uzbekistan, 2026
stories.summary: Tashkent, Uzbekistan, registered 290 invasive meningococcal disease cases during January-April 2026; the case fatality rate was 8.3%. Meningeal signs appeared in only 3.1% of patients and were the sole signs associated with death.

stories.title: Co-occurrence of anaemia and malaria among children under five in Uganda: A joint modeling analysis
stories.summary: Childhood illnesses such as anaemia and malaria continue to pose significant health risks for children under five in sub-Saharan Africa. These conditions often co-occur, reflecting complex interdependencies driven by shared biological and environmental factors.

stories.title: Cocirculation of Human Monkeypox Virus Clade 1b with Varicella Zoster Virus, Uganda
stories.summary: In July 2024, we reported information on the initial human mpox cases in Uganda. Genomic characterization of clinically suspected cases (July-December 2024) revealed cocirculation of several monkeypox virus clade 1b clusters and varicella zoster virus.

stories.title: Conflict May Explain Drop in Ebola Cases, as Amnesty Documents M23 ‘Abuses’ in DRC
stories.summary: The security situation in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) could be behind the significant decline in Ebola cases over the past week, the Africa Centre for Disease Control and Prevention warned on Thursday.

stories.title: Coroner warns of risk of future deaths at mental health unit where patient was killed
stories.summary: Hugo Flint-Cahan, 34, was fatally attacked by Rolando Torres-Pena, 22, at a mental health trust in east London.

stories.title: Could quitting ultra-processed food boost your mental health?
stories.summary: People with depression who dramatically cut ultra-processed foods experienced notable improvements in their symptoms in a small preliminary study. Researchers suspect healthier eating may benefit the brain partly by reducing gut damage and chronic inflammation.

stories.title: Detection of Anaplasma capra in Patients with Suspected Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever, Turkey, 2022
stories.summary: Anaplasma capra is a recently discovered bacterial tickborne pathogen that was first identified in goats in 2012 and later in humans in China in 2015. We detected and genetically characterized A.

stories.title: Detection of Divergent Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza A(H5N1) Clade 2.3.4.4b Virus, São Paulo, Brazil, 2025
stories.summary: In 2025, we detected highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1 virus in dead waterfowl at Ibirapuera Park, São Paulo, Brazil.

stories.title: Detection of Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza A(H5N1) Virus in Cat and Rats during Outbreak in Backyard Poultry, United States, 2025
stories.summary: In 2025, highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) virus was detected in a poultry flock in Illinois, USA. Quantitative reverse transcription PCR, sequencing, and histopathology on cat and rat samples from the farm showed multiple positive tissues and high sequence identity to an avian isolate.

stories.title: Does the messenger make the difference? Perceived reliability of health information sources during the COVID-19 pandemic in multi-ethnic Malaysia
stories.summary: The COVID-19 infodemic highlighted the need to identify the extent to which health information messengers were perceived as reliable by the public in supporting effective public health communication.

stories.title: Early Action Review of Detection, Notification, and Response Timeliness during Cross-Border Bundibugyo Virus Disease Outbreak, Uganda, 2026
stories.summary: Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD), an Ebola virus species with no licensed vaccine or therapeutic, reemerged in May 2026 as a cross-border outbreak in Uganda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

stories.title: Ebola response faces setback as transit centre burns down in DR Congo camp
stories.summary: The enormous challenge of halting the spread of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) just became even harder after a key transit centre for patients requiring treatment burned down in Ituri province.

stories.title: Emergence of Macrolide-Resistant Bordetella pertussis, Peru, 2025
stories.summary: We report the emergence of macrolide-resistant Bordetella pertussis during a pertussis outbreak in Peru. Among 68 cases, 31% carried the A2047G gene mutation, conferring resistance to macrolides.

stories.title: Evaluating smartphone-based cough frequency monitoring for tuberculosis screening and triage in Uganda: A mixed-methods evaluation
stories.summary: Symptom-based tuberculosis screening usually depends on self-reported cough, which is subjective. Passive smartphone cough monitoring offers a more objective alternative.

stories.title: Evaluation of Trichodysplasia Spinulosa Polyomavirus in Skin Biopsies, United States
stories.summary: Trichodysplasia spinulosa polyomavirus (TSPyV) has been identified in human endothelial cell tumors. We evaluated 25 clinical cases of various inflammatory dermatoses in California, USA, for TSPyV by using RNAscope in situ hybridization.

stories.title: Genomic Epidemiology of Salmonella enterica Serovar Hadar Strain Linked to Poultry-Associated Salmonellosis Outbreaks, United States
stories.summary: Nontyphoidal Salmonella enterica serovar Hadar causes poultry-associated salmonellosis outbreaks in the United States. One persisting strain of Salmonella Hadar caused 5 multistate outbreaks resulting in ≈2,000 human cases during 2020-2023.

stories.title: Global plastics treaty negotiations and health-care system use of plastics, WHO African Region
stories.summary: Egbewande OM, Okediji OE, Adeboye AS.

stories.title: Haemophilus ducreyi Bacteria Causing Cutaneous Ulcer Outbreak in Children, Sierra Leone, December 2025
stories.summary: We report a cutaneous ulcer outbreak in Sierra Leone in 2025 that predominantly affected ≈403 schoolchildren. The causative agent was confirmed as Haemophilus ducreyi, a bacterium traditionally associated with the sexually transmitted infection chancroid but more recently recognized as an emerging...

stories.title: Heat-related deaths in Phoenix rise, after two years of decline
stories.summary: Metro Phoenix has so far seen twice as many heat deaths as this time last year. Authorities are trying to understand why and how to intervene.

stories.title: Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza Virus Subtype 5 in Cetaceans, Brazil
stories.summary: We identified highly pathogenic avian influenza virus subtype H5 in stranded dolphins along the coastline of Brazil during 2023-2025. Infected animals included species classified as vulnerable or endangered.

stories.title: Household and community drivers of Aedes aegypti infestation in tropical cities: Guiding community-led interventions
stories.summary: Disadvantaged communities characterised by poor sanitation conditions, overcrowding, and limited vector control are highly susceptible to Aedes aegypti proliferation and arboviral disease transmission. Effective mosquito vector control requires a detailed understanding of Ae.

stories.title: Human Infection with Japanese Encephalitis Virus Genotype V, China, 2025
stories.summary: Japanese encephalitis virus genotype V (JEV GV) has caused multiple cases of viral encephalitis in South Korea. We report a human case of JEV GV in China, confirmed by serology, sequencing, and quantitative reverse transcription PCR.

stories.title: Human Papillomavirus Condylomas of Extragenital Site in Immunocompetent Man, New York, USA, 2025
stories.summary: Human papillomavirus types 6 and 11 are associated with mucosal condylomata acuminata, with rare reports of extragenital manifestations. We report a case of condyloma localized to the neck of an immunocompetent heterosexual man, without concurrent anogenital lesions.

stories.title: Influence of physician and consumer demographics on AI-use penalties in primary care: a vignette-based study
stories.summary: We investigated how the "AI-use penalty"- physicians disclosing AI use being perceived more negatively-is affected by physician and consumer demographics in primary care settings. Participants (N = 1030) assessed fictitious family doctor advertisements varying in AI-use and demographics.

stories.title: International organisations agree on the importance of surveillance, but not on its definition
stories.summary: Holmes IA, Falvo C, Gilbertson K, Willison CE, Singer PM, Greer SL.

stories.title: Knowledge of HIV status in a rural Ugandan population with a sustained, generalised HIV epidemic
stories.summary: For people living with HIV, knowledge of their status is essential to access antiretroviral therapies (ART). This knowledge can be measured by population surveys that record self-reported HIV status before offering HIV testing.

stories.title: Microfilaremic loiasis is associated with T cell hyporesponsiveness against SARS-CoV-2
stories.summary: Loiasis is a chronic filarial infection endemic to Central and West Africa. Although long considered benign, increasing evidence links loiasis to substantial morbidity and mortality.

stories.title: Mistrust in science and a juicy gene-editing lawsuit
stories.summary: Why have so many Americans lost trust in science? And what's the deal with a new gene-editing lawsuit? Find out on this week's episode of "The Readout LOUD" podcast.

stories.title: This common mistake can add nearly 7 points to your blood pressure reading
stories.summary: A common mistake during blood pressure checks could make readings appear substantially higher than they really are. Johns Hopkins researchers found that leaving the arm unsupported can raise systolic readings by about 6.5 mmHg, potentially affecting a hypertension diagnosis.

stories.title: Trump administration appeals ruling blocking limits on international student visas
stories.summary: DHS has appealed a court ruling blocking it from restricting how long international students and postdoctoral researchers can remain in the U.S.

stories.title: 'My big breasts lead to lewd comments in the street'
stories.summary: Charlotte Howard has been turned down for breast reduction surgery by the NHS, despite daily pain.

stories.title: After failed execution, health workers say Tennessee's method flouts medical ethics
stories.summary: After a botched lethal injection in May, dozens of Tennessee medical professionals told the governor that healthcare professionals shouldn't help with executions, no matter the method.

stories.title: Cannabis users were twice as likely to commit violence, review finds
stories.summary: A review of more than 265,000 people found that cannabis use was associated with higher rates of both committing violence and becoming a victim of it. The researchers say the link is significant but does not prove cannabis itself is the cause.

stories.title: Creatine may help build muscle even without exercise, researchers find
stories.summary: Creatine helped middle-aged adults gain muscle and strength even without a structured workout program in a new 12-week study. When combined with exercise and a calorie-reduced diet, it produced even greater strength gains while helping participants add lean tissue and lose fat.

stories.title: Despite the Deadline, US Bilateral Health Deals Are Not Ready for Implementation
stories.summary: Although the United States’ bilateral health memorandums of understanding (MOUs) with 35 countries are due to come into effect on Thursday (1 October), the start of the US fiscal year, the money will not flow yet – as countries have until Friday to submit their final 2027 budgets.

stories.title: Drugs are widely used to sedate dementia patients. Her sons wanted to keep her off them
stories.summary: Potent sedating medications are often used on agitated people with dementia in long-term care facilities despite federal efforts to discourage them. A clash over whether to drug a Michigan woman illuminates the wrenching decisions families and guardians face.

stories.title: Inside India's forest villages, where a dangerous mix of crises led to 32 child deaths
stories.summary: At least 32 children have died in India's Balaghat district since May amid outbreaks of measles and malaria.

stories.title: Montana starts enforcing Medicaid work requirements on Oct 1. Patients are confused
stories.summary: In most states, people with Medicaid coverage will have to prove they're working, volunteering or studying, starting Jan. 1. But Montana is starting that early, and it's sowing confusion and anxiety.

stories.title: Travel plans? Here's what to know as measles exposures reach trains and games
stories.summary: Measles is traveling, with outbreaks in Pennsylvania, Ohio and New York, and exposures on transportation and in sports. What should you know before getting on a plane or train?

stories.title: What's behind HHS claims that gender-affirming care 'may' radicalize
stories.summary: The report is the agency's latest effort to chip away at trust in established health care models for transgender people. Critics say it frames transgender identity as illegitimate or even dangerous.

stories.title: Brain scans reveal which disorders are linked to faster brain aging
stories.summary: A massive MRI study found that Alzheimer’s disease, mild cognitive impairment, psychiatric disorders, and addiction are associated with distinct patterns of accelerated brain aging.

stories.title: Burnham vows to end existing pension triple lock in 2030 to help fund care
stories.summary: The PM was at times emotional during his conference speech in which he outlined his long-term plan for the UK.

stories.title: Children at risk for depression get “stuck” on sad faces
stories.summary: Depression may change which emotional faces children notice most, but the pattern appears to depend on family history. Children at higher familial risk became increasingly focused on sad faces, while lower-risk children with rising symptoms paid less attention to happy ones.

stories.title: DRC: Early access to care and oxygen decisive for Ebola patients’ survival – WHO
stories.summary: In the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), health workers fighting the country’s largest-ever Ebola outbreak are struggling to overcome critical challenges to patient care, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) warned on Tuesday.

stories.title: Forget LASIK: Safer, cheaper vision correction without lasers or incisions
stories.summary: Scientists are developing a possible alternative to LASIK that reshapes the cornea without cutting it or using a laser. The technique uses a small electric potential and a specially shaped platinum lens to temporarily soften the cornea, allowing it to be molded in about a minute.

stories.title: MPP Signs Multiple Regional Agreements to Expand Access to Flu Antiviral Medicine
stories.summary: The Medicines Patent Pool (MPP) has signed sublicense agreements with 11 manufacturers across multiple regions to expand access to generic baloxavir marboxil, a single-dose antiviral treatment for influenza that was originally developed by Swiss pharmaceutical company Roche.

stories.title: Renewed Fighting in Yemen Brings Increased Cholera, Measles and Dengue
stories.summary: Thousands of people displaced by conflict in Yemen are at risk of cholera, measles, malaria and dengue as the El Niño season approaches, the World Health Organization’s (WHO) Eastern Mediterranean region warned this week.

stories.title: Scientists find new virus behind mysterious tick illness
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered a new tick-borne virus in China that causes flu-like illness and may account for previously unexplained cases of fever, fatigue, digestive problems, and low platelet counts.

stories.title: 160-million-year-old proteins show surprising power against superbugs
stories.summary: Scientists resurrected antimicrobial peptides from mammals that lived millions of years ago and found that some were more potent against drug-resistant bacteria than modern human versions.

stories.title: Blood tests reveal why astronauts get constipated in space
stories.summary: Spaceflight may dramatically change the gut within weeks, causing bacteria to break down more protein as food moves more slowly through the intestines.

stories.title: DR Congo Ebola emergency: Calls grow for urgent humanitarian access
stories.summary: Aid teams trying to keep deadly Ebola disease from spreading in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) are increasingly concerned about ongoing fighting and violence that has forced thousands of people to flee a displacement camp in the vast, resource-rich east of the country.

stories.title: DRC politician beaten to death after radio appearance about Ebola outbreak
stories.summary: Marie-Celestin Karondwa was attacked on Sunday after promoting measures to prevent spread of disease, his party says A senior member of the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s ruling party was beaten to death on Sunday after appearing on a radio programme to raise awareness about the Ebola outbreak,...

stories.title: New NHS-style social care system could take decades, Dilnot says
stories.summary: Sir Andrew Dilnot, who proposed reforms 15 years ago, says the cost of such a scheme would be "very substantial".

stories.title: Ten NHS staff removed over Noah Woods data breach
stories.summary: East Suffolk and North Essex NHS Foundation Trust says it has launched an "urgent" investigation.

stories.title: The Health Case for Investment in Clean Air in Africa
stories.summary: Lisa Sama is a 19-year-old medical student in Cameroon. As far back as she can remember, she has lived with asthma, and in recent years, she has turned her attention to the role that air pollution plays in her health.

stories.title: US response to UN pandemic talks ‘severely weakens’ global planning, says leading health expert
stories.summary: The US says it is unable to support a major global text on pandemic prevention and preparedness put forward at UN general assembly The United States government’s decision to block a major global declaration on pandemic preparedness “severely weakens” the effort, and signals intent to disrupt...

stories.title: 'Broken social care will in the end break the NHS,' says Burnham
stories.summary: Andy Burnham said the proposed care service would be laid out in detail and put on the ballot at the next general election.

stories.title: NHS to suspend staff suspected of snooping on patient records
stories.summary: There have been too many cases of staff abusing patient trust, and enough is enough, the head of the NHS in England says.

stories.title: NHS staff investigated over access to dead teenager's medical records
stories.summary: Oliver McGowan, who died in 2016, may have had his medical records accessed inappropriately after his death by NHS staff in Bristol.

stories.title: DR Congo Ebola outbreak toll exceeds 3,700 deaths
stories.summary: More than 130 days into the latest Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), health experts said on Wednesday that response efforts have been scaled up significantly and “the first encouraging signs of progress” are now being seen.

stories.title: As president of Botswana, I know how we can make malaria a memory in Africa | Duma Gideon Boko
stories.summary: The disease is soaring as funding is cut. African nations are plugging the gap but they need help with the transition Botswana nearly defeated malaria. In 2024, we recorded just 290 cases and one death.

stories.title: ‘I lost my children, and I’m afraid of losing my baby again’: a day in the life of a pregnant woman in Gaza
stories.summary: Alaa lives in a tent pitched on the ruins of her house, which was destroyed by an Israeli airstrike that killed all three of her children. In one month, she will give birth again.

stories.title: Ebola vaccine research programme begins in DR Congo
stories.summary: An Ebola vaccine programme is underway in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), involving frontline health workers and others involved in the response.

stories.title: Women and girls pay high price in DR Congo Ebola outbreak
stories.summary: The deadly Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has taken a disproportionate toll on women and girls, many of whom are on the frontlines caring for patients as well as their own families despite the high risk of infection.

stories.title: Ebola outbreak in DRC has peaked, say authorities, as infection rates slow
stories.summary: Almost 3,500 people have died in outbreak and experts say more must be done to ensure Bundibugyo is under control Authorities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo have announced that the Ebola outbreak ravaging parts of the country has reached its peak.

stories.title: Ebola responders grapple with widening outbreak in DR Congo
stories.summary: The deadly Ebola virus outbreak in DR Congo continues to spread across the vast country despite some success in containing it, aid officials said on Tuesday, in a renewed call for international support to help responders on the ground.
